findings.name: Average_mosaic_260620_wrought_316L_fatigue_900_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: One faint, short dark streak entering the material horizontally from the specimen edge near mid-height (approx x 195-265, y 285-305 in raw-panel coords), with a slight downward branch - consistent with an edge/notch-initiated fatigue crack tip. Nothing crack-like anywhere in the bulk of the illuminated material; the rest of the frame is only the regular rectangular mosaic-tile grid plus a broad illumination gradient.
findings.notes: Wrought 316L H Fatigue, 900 cycles - the group this model is known to over-predict on. Measured: the left 32.5% of the raw panel is dead black (column means ~3.5/255), i.e. off-specimen empty field with a near-vertical specimen edge running top-to-bottom at about x=32% of the panel width. Red covers 63.9% of the overlay panel overall (matches the reported area 0.6445, 242 regions), but 86.8% of that left empty field is painted red as a single solid slab, and red still covers 53% of the genuine specimen area, tracking the mosaic tile seams and the merely-darker upper-right tiles rather than any linear defect. The one plausible real crack at the specimen edge is completely buried inside the solid red slab, so it is indistinguishable from the flooded empty field - the prediction carries essentially no usable signal. Classic 'broad dark region = crack' failure. Recommendation: mask the off-specimen background (threshold on the near-zero intensity region) before scoring, and flat-field/de-tile to suppress the mosaic seam and vignetting response; do not use this frame's mask as pseudo-label training data.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260620_wrought_316L_fatigue_0_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: none visible - this is a 0_cycles (undamaged) specimen; the only structure is the smooth rounded bright specimen boundary at left and the regular mosaic-tile grid. No elongated dark connected feature anywhere in the material.
findings.notes: Wrought 316L H Fatigue, 0 cycles = UNDAMAGED, so the reported 0.410 area fraction and 256 regions are essentially 100% false positive. Two distinct failure modes stacked: (1) a solid red lobe filling the entire near-black left ~40% of the frame (out-of-field / off-specimen air), bounded exactly by the curved specimen silhouette, which proves the model is thresholding on absolute darkness; (2) inside the specimen the red tracks the periodic rectangular mosaic-tile seams - the repeating ~5x5 lattice of red blobs and vertical bars is spatially locked to the tile grid, not to material features. This frame is a prime candidate for exclusion or for use as a hard negative.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260618_b2_337_19_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: Two dark elongated features: (a) an upper band starting mid-left-of-center and running diagonally up-right to the right edge, diffuse/lobed with wispy branch tips; (b) a lower, sharper horizontal band entering at the left edge and running across the lower-middle third, darkest near center with a short downward branch at ~60% width. Both are clearly dark relative to their local mid-gray surroundings and sit in material that has visible mottled texture, so they read as genuine crack/damage, not vignetting.
findings.notes: B2 316L H Tension = the model's own training group, and localization is broadly correct: red sits on the two dark bands, not on the bright corners. Predicted area 0.277 (10 regions). Failure mode is dilation rather than wholesale false positives: the red mask is a smoothed, fattened version of each band, so it swallows the mid-gray halo around the dark cores and merges across the gap between the two bands in the right half, filling nearly the whole upper-right quadrant including areas only slightly darker than background. The isolated red blob at lower-right (~85% width, ~85% height) sits on a mottled mid-gray patch with no distinct elongated dark core — likely false positive. Small near-black wedge at the right edge (mid-height) is ambiguous: it could be the crack exiting the field of view or the specimen boundary/out-of-field; red covers it either way, but it is a small fraction of the frame.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260618_b2_340_00_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260620_b3_362_50um_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260620_b3_380_00um_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260620_b3_380_94um_ZOOM_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim

The plausible true crack is ~4% of the frame, so this is roughly a 5x over-prediction: red forms one solid blob filling the whole right-center quadrant (x~45%-100%, y~27%-88%) instead of a crack-shaped line. Also note this frame is extremely smooth/blurred - high-frequency std is only 5.2 gray levels vs global std 52.6, so there is almost no microstructural texture to distinguish crack from shadow. findings.name: Average_mosaic_260620_b3_388_13um_LARGE_2_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim

findings.notes: Best-behaved frame of the seven and the best training candidate. Predicted area 24.2% (measured red 0.241) and the red genuinely follows the crack: mean gray under red is 68 vs 200 outside, and precision against a local-contrast dark mask is 0.64-0.71 (roughly double every other frame here). Failure mode is inflation of crack THICKNESS rather than location - red bleeds ~2x beyond the dark band vertically and adds a fringe of small blobs above/below and a scattered row of specks near the bottom edge (hence 103 regions). Note the mosaic-tile grid is clearly visible as horizontal banding across the top and bottom thirds; it is correctly NOT being labeled, apart from the low blob row that lines up with one tile seam. Plausible true crack ~12%, so ~2x over-prediction.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260620_b3_388_13um_ZOOM_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: Same crack as 53.png at higher zoom: a dark wavy band crossing the full width at roughly y=40-65%, dipping lowest around x=25-35%. Genuinely dark and elongated, so a real crack, but its upper and lower boundaries fade smoothly into surrounding gray with no texture to bound them.
findings.notes: Worst over-prediction of the six specimen-bearing frames: predicted area 44.1% (measured red 0.437) - nearly half the frame painted as crack, in a single contiguous slab spanning left edge to right edge with only 9 regions. 8.2% of pixels are <20/255 and 24.5% <100/255; mean gray under red is 93 vs 204 outside; precision against a local-contrast dark mask is only 0.38, i.e. the red is ~2x the area of anything locally dark. Plausible true crack ~10%, so ~4.4x over-prediction. Same field of view as 53.png, so 53/54 are correlated; 53's mask is far more usable than 54's.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260620_b3_3_0lbf_268_13um_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: none visible - the frame is empty field. The only signal is a small bright cloud in the top-left corner (roughly x=0-40%, top 20% of the frame, with one saturated white lobe); the remaining ~90% of the frame is flat black with no structure whatsoever.
findings.unusable_reason: Nearly the entire frame is empty/black: 93.9% of pixels are below 20/255 and the mean gray level is 9.8. There is no discernible specimen material and no texture to learn from - only a small transmitted-beam blob in the top-left corner. This looks like a failed/mis-positioned acquisition (or the specimen almost entirely out of field). Drop it from training and from any area-fraction statistics.
findings.notes: THIS IS THE HEADLINE FAILURE. Predicted crack area 87.6% (measured red 0.870): the model paints the entire black field red and leaves only the bright top-left blob unlabeled - it has literally inverted into a 'dark = crack' brightness threshold. Mean gray under the red mask is 3.5/255, i.e. it is labeling pure void as crack. Two independent reasons this is a guaranteed false positive: (1) the frame contains no specimen, and (2) the name is '3_0lbf' - zero applied load, an UNDAMAGED baseline, so the true crack area should be ~0. Recommend excluding 55.png from the dataset entirely and adding an automatic pre-filter that rejects frames whose mean intensity or fraction-of-nonblack falls below a threshold (e.g. reject if >70% of pixels < 20/255), since a single frame like this contributes ~0.87 area fraction and will badly distort any aggregate metric.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260618_B2_2_9_lbf_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of005.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: none visible - only the regular 6x5 mosaic-tile grid, a broad illumination gradient darkening toward the bottom, and the curved specimen edge on the right
findings.notes: B2 316L H Tension (training group), 9 lbf, predicted area 0.359. Measured: 20.7% of the frame is near-black off-specimen field on the right (curved specimen boundary); 86% of that black band is painted red, and 48.7% of ALL red pixels sit on it, so roughly half the predicted 'crack' is pure empty space. The remaining ~19% of frame is on-specimen red that traces the darker mosaic-tile seams/intersections and the vignetted bottom rows (a solid red strip runs along the whole bottom edge), not any elongated feature. Mean gray under red is 49 vs 151 elsewhere but mean local contrast under red is only -4.7, i.e. the model is keying on absolute darkness/vignetting, not local crack contrast. Needs a field/specimen mask plus flat-field correction before use.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260618_B2_333_75_um_zoom_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: two roughly horizontal, connected, branching dark bands through the middle of the frame - an upper one running from mid-left to the right edge with a very dark concentrated core right of center, and a lower one across the left-center - plus a small satellite lobe at lower-center-right; textured material on all sides
findings.notes: B2 316L H Tension, 333.75 um zoom step, predicted area 0.276 with only 19 regions. Only 1.6% of the frame is near-black and just 4.8% of red pixels land there, so essentially all red is on specimen material. Red follows the branching topology of the dark bands correctly, including the bright gap between upper and lower branches. Mean gray under red 130 vs 192 elsewhere; mean local contrast under red -13.8 vs +5.2 elsewhere, confirming it locks onto genuinely locally-dark features. Only caveat: about 36% of red pixels sit in the diffuse fringe (local contrast > -5), so the mask is somewhat dilated beyond the dark core into the projection halo - it over-states crack width but not crack location. This is the kind of frame the model was trained on and it behaves well here.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260618_B2_3_1_lbf_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: none visible - the frame is the mosaic tile grid plus a smooth brightness gradient; the only linear features are the regular horizontal and vertical tile seams
findings.notes: B2 316L H Tension, 1 lbf (essentially undamaged, should have almost no crack), predicted area 0.232 with 288 regions. 15.6% of the frame is off-specimen near-black on the right and 83% of it is red; 54% of all red pixels are on that empty band. The on-specimen red is a textbook grid false positive: beads along the darker mosaic-tile seams and at seam intersections, including one conspicuous vertical red stripe on a tile boundary in the upper right that could easily be mistaken for a detected crack. The 288-region count is itself a red flag - real cracks are a few connected components, not hundreds of seam fragments. Not usable for evaluation as-is without a field mask and tile-seam suppression.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260618_B2_3_2_lbf_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: no convincing crack - many small faint dark elongated flecks/streaks scattered through the material (mostly horizontal, short) that look like surface marks, pores or mosaic-stitch artifacts rather than a connected crack, plus a small dark notch where the specimen edge meets the black field at mid-height on the right
findings.notes: B2 316L H Tension, 2 lbf (near-undamaged), predicted area 0.216 with 255 regions. 13.9% of the frame is off-specimen near-black on the right, 83% of it painted red, and 51.5% of all red pixels sit there as a solid red slab down the right side. The on-specimen red is better targeted than in 28/30 (mean local contrast under red -10.7, and the flecks it paints do correspond to visible dark streaks), so it is not purely a brightness response - but flecks are not a crack, and there is still substantial red along tile seams and the vignetted bottom edge. At 2 lbf the correct answer is near-zero crack area, so the reported 0.216 is dominated by false positive.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260618_B2_amb_mosaic_2_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of005.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: none visible - unloaded ambient reference: bright material with the 4x5 mosaic tile grid and vignetting, and a strongly curved specimen boundary running top-to-bottom on the right
findings.notes: B2 316L H Tension ambient/unloaded reference, predicted area 0.261 with 86 regions. Worst signal-to-noise case of this set: 25.2% of the frame is off-specimen near-black, 87% of that band is red, and 83% of ALL red pixels lie on it. Subtracting the band leaves only about 4.5% of the frame as on-specimen red (small blobs hugging the specimen edge and a few tile intersections in the lower half). So the headline 0.261 crack fraction is almost entirely the empty field being classified as crack, on a frame that should read ~0. Because the boundary is a smooth curve, a simple threshold-based field mask would remove nearly all of the error here.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260618_b2_335_31um_FRFR_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: same crack system as 29 but more open: a strong upper branch sweeping from left-center to the right edge with a near-black core just right of center, and a distinctly darker, well-defined lower branch running horizontally across the left half, plus a separate lobe at lower-right; textured material all around them
findings.notes: B2 316L H Tension, 335.31 um displacement step (same specimen/location as 29 and 34, one load increment later - crack is visibly darker and wider). Predicted area 0.271 with only 14 regions, the right order of magnitude for a few connected crack branches. Just 2.2% of the frame is near-black and only 7.8% of red pixels touch it; 98% of the dark material is covered. Mean gray under red 117 vs 185 elsewhere, local contrast -15.6 vs +5.8. Red tracks both branches and their connectivity faithfully. Same mild caveat as 29/34: ~37% of red pixels are in the low-contrast diffuse fringe, so the upper-right lobe in particular is fatter than the visibly dark core - width over-stated, location and topology right. Good frame, good prediction.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260618_b2_336_25_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: most developed stage of the same crack: upper branch from mid-left to the right edge terminating in a nearly black wedge right of center, a thick dark lower branch across the left-center that thins toward the right, and a detached lower-right lobe; clear textured material above and below both branches
findings.notes: B2 316L H Tension, 336.25 um displacement (one step past 33), predicted area 0.283 with 21 regions. Only 1.7% of the frame is near-black and just 5.5% of red pixels land there, so the prediction is essentially all on-specimen; 90% of the dark material is covered. Mean gray under red 124 vs 191 elsewhere, local contrast -14.9 vs +5.9. Red follows both branches and the detached lobe and correctly leaves the bright band between them unpainted. Same dilation caveat as 29/33 (~36% of red in the diffuse fringe). Side note worth checking: predicted area is nearly flat across 29 (0.276) -> 33 (0.271) -> 34 (0.283) even though the crack visibly opens, suggesting fringe dilation inflates the early step and flattens the growth curve.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_200_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: none visible. Only a small dark pit/notch right at the specimen silhouette edge at ~55% frame height; no elongated feature runs into the textured material. Consistent with only 200 fatigue cycles.
findings.notes: AM 316LH Fatigue, 200 cycles. Left ~30% of the frame is a flat, featureless saturated-dark silhouette (grip/shoulder shadow or out-of-field) with a smooth lobed boundary; a thin dark strip also runs down the right edge. Only the right ~2/3 carries resolvable mosaic-tile texture. Measured red fraction 0.68 (matches reported area 0.680). Diagnostic: 83% of all sub-45 gray pixels are red vs 16% of the brightest quartile, and 38% of every red pixel lies in the off-specimen dark region. The red boundary in the material simply traces the top-dark/bottom-bright illumination gradient, not any feature. Recommend excluding or masking the left third before use as training data.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_400_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: borderline / not a true crack: a distinct dark wedge-shaped notch sits at the specimen edge at ~48% height, but nothing elongated propagates from it into the textured material.
findings.notes: AM 316LH Fatigue, 400 cycles. Left ~25-30% is flat dark off-specimen with a round protruding lobe. Two perfectly uniform horizontal stripes inside that dark band are detector/mosaic banding artifacts, NOT cracks. Measured red 0.61 (reported 0.611). 86% of the dark region is red, 18% of all red is off-specimen. Most damning: the in-material red traces the rectangular mosaic tile-seam lattice almost exactly, and the reported 441 regions is just that seam network broken into fragments. The whole right-edge column is also flooded.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_600_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: none visible. The large dark area is a smooth, completely featureless silhouette with a bright refraction halo along its curved boundary - a specimen edge, not a crack.
findings.notes: AM 316LH Fatigue, 600 cycles. Worst frame of this batch and the strongest exclusion candidate: 56-60% of the frame is flat saturated dark occupying the entire upper-left diagonal (left third is 95% near-black, top third 88%). Only the lower-right ~40% has resolvable material. Measured red 0.77 (reported 0.773) - the highest in the set - and the red mask is essentially 'everything above the specimen silhouette'. 92% of dark pixels are red and 72% of ALL red pixels are off-specimen. Recommend dropping this frame or cropping to the lower-right quadrant.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_700_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: a genuine faint crack: a thin dark filament emerging from the notch on the specimen edge at ~38% frame height, running rightward and slightly downward for roughly 20% of the frame width, with slight branching. Only apparent after local contrast enhancement.
findings.notes: AM 316LH Fatigue, 700 cycles. Left ~20-25% is flat dark off-specimen; thin dark strip on the right edge; the top of the material is dimmed by vignetting but is still specimen. Measured red 0.56 (reported 0.562). The overlay floods the entire top half plus the left dark band - 74% of dark pixels and 51% of material pixels are red - so the one real crack filament is swallowed inside the flood rather than resolved. This frame has genuine ground truth worth labelling by hand.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_800_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: clearest real crack in this batch: a thin, dark, branching filament starting at the edge notch at ~38-42% frame height and extending right into the material for ~25% of the frame width, with secondary short branches above and below the main path.
findings.notes: AM 316LH Fatigue, 800 cycles. Left ~25% flat dark off-specimen silhouette, plus a dark vignetted band across the top and a dark column at the right edge. Measured red 0.51 (reported 0.511). Red covers the left dark strip, the whole top band, the right-edge column, and traces every mosaic tile seam; 79% of dark pixels are red vs 12% of the brightest quartile, and 42% of all red is off-specimen. Net effect: the real crack is indistinguishable because it sits inside a large red flood. Best candidate in this batch for hand-labelled positive training data.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_900_cycles_FRFR_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: a real crack: thin dark branching filament emerging from the edge notch at ~60% frame height and running rightward into the material for ~25% of the frame width; clearly resolved after local contrast enhancement.
findings.notes: AM 316LH Fatigue, 900 cycles. Wide-aspect frame. Left ~15-20% is a flat dark lobed off-specimen silhouette with a saturated bright wedge at the top-left corner. Measured red 0.53 (reported 0.523). This frame is the single clearest proof the model learned the acquisition artifact rather than damage: the red mask forms an almost perfect rectangular lattice coinciding with the mosaic tile seams, leaving only the bright tile centres unpainted, plus the entire left dark region. 75% of dark pixels red vs 23% of the brightest quartile. The actual crack filament gets no distinct treatment.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260618_B2_2_1_lbf_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of005.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: none visible. Only faint inclusion/porosity speckle and one very faint short squiggle near the bottom-centre. This is a 1 lbf (essentially unloaded) tension specimen, so it should be crack-free.
findings.notes: B2 316L H Tension, 1 lbf - the model's own training group, and visibly the best-behaved frame. Bright textured specimen fills the left ~72% with a smooth necked edge; the right ~25% is off-specimen background (right third is 75% near-black). Measured red 0.39 (reported 0.388). Failure mode here is structured rather than global: only 22% of material pixels are red, but 89% of the off-specimen dark band is red and 58% of ALL red pixels sit in that non-specimen band, plus a solid red strip along the bottom edge and blobs following the tile seams. Since this specimen is undamaged, every red pixel here is a false positive - so the residual error even in-domain is dominated by off-specimen flooding and mosaic-seam pickup.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_1400_cycles_tip_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: Single thin dark filament entering the LEFT edge at ~55% height, running right and slightly upward, splaying into fine multi-strand branches around x=25-45% of width, then terminating (crack tip) near frame center. Confined to the left ~45% of the frame; total real crack area is on the order of 1-2% of pixels.
findings.notes: Predicted area 0.707 vs a realistic ~1-2% -> roughly 40x over-prediction. Raw panel has a monotonic left-to-right / bottom-to-top brightness decay (column-bin means 150 -> 18 of 255); the red mask lands almost exactly on the dark side of that gradient and essentially ignores the actual crack filament, which sits in the bright left-central region. A single global brightness threshold (I<155) reproduces 84.5% of the red mask pixel-for-pixel, confirming the model is thresholding illumination, not detecting cracks. High-pass local texture std collapses from 10.1 (leftmost sixth) to 1.9 (rightmost sixth), i.e. the flooded region is flat and featureless with no elongated structures to find. 14.8% of the frame is genuinely near-black out-of-field (top-right corner plus a strip along the right edge, visible as a noise-amplified boundary in a flat-fielded version), and 72% of that out-of-field area is painted red. Frame is usable for training but needs an out-of-field mask on the right/top-right AND per-image flat-field correction before labels are trustworthy.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_1450_cycles_tip_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: Dark branching filament entering the LEFT edge at ~40% height, running right and rising; splits into a fan of fine parallel strands around x=45-70% of width and reaches roughly 75% of the frame width before fading. Clearly elongated and connected; real area ~1-2% of pixels.
findings.notes: Predicted area 0.676 vs realistic ~1-2% -> ~35-50x over-prediction. Same left-bright/right-black gradient (column-bin means 165 -> 19). A plain global threshold I<140 reproduces 83.3% of the red mask, so the prediction is effectively a brightness cut. Local texture std falls 10.2 -> 1.7 left-to-right, so the flooded right side contains no crack-like structure. 9.2% of the frame is near-black out-of-field (right edge band plus top-right corner) and 65% of it is red. The real crack, which extends further right than in 07, is only partially and inconsistently covered while the surrounding non-crack dark field is fully covered.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_1650_cycles_tip_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: The most developed crack in this set: a strong dark branching feature entering the LEFT edge at ~45% height, running right, then bifurcating into an upward branch that climbs to the upper right (reaching x=70-90% of width) and a shallower branch continuing horizontally. Clearly connected and elongated across most of the frame width; real area ~2-3% of pixels.
findings.notes: Predicted area 0.631 vs realistic ~2-3% -> ~20-30x over-prediction. Strongest gradient of the set (column-bin means 202 -> 17). Global threshold I<155 reproduces 85.5% of the red mask. Texture std 19.1 -> 1.7 left-to-right. 5.9% of the frame is near-black out-of-field (right edge strip and top-right corner) and 86% of that is painted red. The red block covers the whole right ~60% as one solid mass, so the genuine rising branch on the right is swallowed rather than resolved - the mask carries no usable crack geometry even where a crack really exists.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_1450_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: Textbook crack: a dark, connected, roughly horizontal feature at mid-height running from the left edge (adjacent to the dark lobe/notch) rightward past ~70% of the frame width, with a distinct Y-fork at x=20-25% and thinner secondary branches above and below. Real area ~2% of pixels.
findings.notes: Predicted area 0.590 vs realistic ~2% -> ~30x over-prediction. Red does partially trace the real crack here (better than the 'tip' frames), but it also fills the entire right ~45% of the frame as one solid block where local texture std is only 1.4-2.9 versus 17.7 on the bright left - i.e. no elongated features exist there at all. Global threshold I<105 reproduces 78.7% of the red mask. Non-specimen area is small: only 2.9% of the frame is near-black (the dark lobe at the left edge) and just 29% of that is red, so masking out-of-field will NOT fix this frame - the false positives are on valid but under-exposed specimen. Fix is flat-field / local-contrast normalization plus negative examples from dark smooth regions.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_1500_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: Connected horizontal crack at mid-height running from the left edge lobe rightward to ~70% of width, with a Y-fork near x=15-20% and a faint branch angling up to the right. Real area ~2% of pixels.
findings.notes: Predicted area 0.594 vs realistic ~2% -> ~30x over-prediction. Same pattern as 08: red follows the crack reasonably in the bright left third, then the right ~40% is a solid red slab over a smooth dark gradient (column-bin means 168 -> 34, texture std 16.3 -> 2.5). Global threshold I<105 reproduces 78.9% of the red mask. Only 2.5% of the frame is near-black out-of-field (left-edge lobe) and 21% of it is red, so the dominant error is false positives on real, in-field, dark specimen rather than on empty field.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_1600_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: Clear mid-height horizontal crack from the left edge running right to ~70% of width, with a pronounced Y-fork at x=10-20% and a thin branch rising toward the upper right around x=55-70%. Confirmed on a flat-fielded rendering. Real area ~2% of pixels.
findings.notes: Predicted area 0.616 vs realistic ~2% -> ~30x over-prediction. Column-bin means 172 -> 28; texture std 18.4 -> 2.5. Global threshold I<100 reproduces 78.3% of the red mask. Red covers the right ~40% solidly plus a vertical red band hugging the left edge next to the dark lobe. Only 2.8% of the frame is near-black out-of-field and 19% of that is red, so non-specimen masking is not the remedy; illumination normalization is. Note also the regular rectangular mosaic-tile grid is strongly visible in this frame and the red mask partly keys onto the darker tile seams, another non-crack artifact being learned as positive.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_1650_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: Connected branching crack at mid-height running from the left edge rightward to ~65-75% of width, with a fork near x=15-20% and an upward-angling branch in the right half. Real area ~2% of pixels.
findings.notes: Predicted area 0.578 vs realistic ~2% -> ~30x over-prediction. Brightest-to-darkest column-bin means 178 -> 34; texture std 20.3 -> 2.8. Global threshold I<105 reproduces 80.0% of the red mask, so this prediction carries almost no information beyond image brightness. Cleanest frame of the set in terms of non-specimen contamination: only 2.1% near-black and 14% of that red. The red does partially trace the real crack in the bright left half, so this frame plus 08/10/11 would make good retraining candidates once the right-side slab false positives are painted out.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_1000_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: Faint thin branching dark line emanating from the notch on the left specimen edge at mid-height (~45% down), running right and slightly down for ~25-30% of the frame width. Visible only under local-contrast enhancement.
findings.notes: Left ~15-18% of the panel is empty field / off-specimen (column means 2-5 of 255, 100% of pixels <25 in the first tenth of the width); the specimen boundary is the bright curved arc. Rest of the frame is a clean 5x4 mosaic-tile grid with bright tile centres and dark seams. Predicted area 0.498 (131 regions). The red mask is essentially the photographic negative of tile-centre brightness: it covers the whole left empty field (65-80% of those columns are red) and the entire rectilinear tile-seam lattice, leaving only tile centres unpainted. Real crack area here is on the order of 1%, so ~50x over-prediction. Out-of-domain group (AM 316LH Fatigue).

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_1100_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: Clear dark, roughly horizontal, branching crack starting at the left specimen notch at mid-height and running right ~40-45% of the frame width, with several fine hair-like branches above and below the main filament.
findings.notes: Left ~14% of the panel is empty field (col means near 0, dark fraction 1.0 in first tenth). Predicted area 0.463 (104 regions). One credit: a red blob does sit roughly over the crack corridor at mid-left, but it is grossly dilated (tens of pixels wide vs a few-pixel crack). Everything else is false positive: the entire left empty field plus the full mosaic tile-seam lattice across all 5x3 tiles. Severe over-prediction of the classic 'dark region = crack' kind.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_1200_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: Thin wispy near-horizontal dark filament from the left notch at ~40% height, extending right ~55-60% of the frame width; forks into two faint strands in its middle third.
findings.notes: Left ~14% empty field. Predicted area 0.364 (140 regions) - the lowest red fraction of these seven, but still severe: the crack itself is ~1% of the frame. The overlay is the most visually diagnostic of the failure mode in this batch - the red traces the regular rectangular mosaic-tile seam grid almost perfectly (grid lines are unmistakable in the overlay), plus the whole left empty field (64-76% red in the first two column bins). Red on the actual crack is incidental.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_1250_cycles_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim
findings.real_crack_description: Faint thin horizontal dark line low in the frame: starts at the left edge at ~88% height and runs right for ~30% of the width, just above the bright bottom band. Weakest real crack signal of the seven.
findings.notes: Specimen material fills essentially the whole frame - mosaic-tile texture is still resolvable at the right edge under a global stretch. Non-specimen is limited to thin edges: a dark top edge band (a few rows) and the outer ~3% of the right edge; not large. Predicted area 0.637 (43 regions). The red mask covers the entire upper ~55% of the frame (87-93% red in row bins 1-3) and the dimmer right side (81-83% red in column bins 7-8), which exactly tracks the broad top-dark / bottom-bright illumination gradient - not a crack feature. findings.reasoning: Measured the red mask and compared it against a local-mean-subtracted version of the raw panel. Red covers 59.6% of the prediction panel. A real crack does exist and the reviewer's geometry is accurate: a thin dark elongated feature at mid-height from x~10% to x~65-70% of width, with a Y-fork near the left and a faint branch angling up-right; its area is only ~1.5-2.5% of pixels. Everything else red is false: (1) a solid rectangular flood filling x>=300 to the right edge, top to bottom, where red is 86-100% but only 1.5% of pixels are darker than their local surroundings and local texture std collapses to 5.1 vs 14.2 on the left half - beyond x~360 the strongest local darkening is -4 gray levels, i.e. no feature at all, yet it is 100% red; this is the smooth illumination falloff / large featureless dark area; (2) two tall vertical red bands at x~15-20% and x~30-35% tracing vertical mosaic tile seams; (3) a vertical red stripe hugging the bright/dark boundary of the left-edge lobe; (4) the mid-height band that does sit on the real crack is dilated to roughly 4-5x the crack's true width. Only 10% of red pixels are even locally dark, and that 10% still includes tile-grid seams. So TP/red is at most ~2.5/59.6, giving ~96% false positive. I agree with over_predicts_severely but disagree with usable=true: a mask dominated by a half-frame flood over featureless dark gradient would teach the model that low intensity equals crack, so this frame is not usable as training data. On red_floods_nonspecimen the reviewer's 'false' is only technically defensible - the thin outer black frame margin is spared - but the flood does blanket a large empty/low-signal region, which is the same failure mode in spirit.

I put it at ~0.98: roughly 98% of the red overlay is false positive, driven by the smooth left-to-right illumination gradient, the rectangular tile-mosaic grid, and the uniformly dark non-specimen border.

USABILITY: I disagree that this should be called unusable, and I agree with the prior reviewer's usable=true. The raw left image is good quality and contains one unambiguous, well-localized crack that a human can trace; nothing about the raw frame is degenerate. The prediction is catastrophically wrong, but that makes the frame a high-value correction/hard-negative example (dark background + tile grid mistaken for crack), not a discard. PREDICTION (right): Red covers 53,505 of 145,600 px = 36.7% of the panel. Breakdown: 16,965 red px (31.7% of all red) fall in the uniformly black non-specimen region on the left (gray < 45) - the model floods the empty area outside the specimen, confirming red_floods_nonspecimen=true. The remaining 36,540 red px inside the specimen are almost entirely the rectangular mosaic tile grid: every vertical and horizontal tile seam of the 5x3 mosaic is painted, plus a 1-px border rectangle around the whole frame, so the red is effectively the set-complement of the bright tile interiors. Independently verified by splitting the panels (left 0-520, right 528-1048), extracting the red mask (r>150,g<90,b<90), and illumination-normalizing the raw panel (divide by sigma=25 Gaussian) plus a fine-scale ridge filter (DoG sigma 1 vs 6) to isolate genuine dark elongated features.

Real crack: CONFIRMED and it is the best-defined crack of the set, but the previous reviewer overstated its extent. Connected-component analysis of the ridge response gives four coherent elongated components: x=0.00-0.18 / y=0.47-0.53 (entry at left edge), x=0.16-0.57 / y=0.35-0.49 (main run rightward, slightly rising), then a bifurcation into x=0.58-0.70 / y=0.16-0.30 (upward branch) and x=0.57-0.68 / y=0.32-0.38 (shallower branch). Total = 3,491 px = 1.8% of specimen; with a generous diffuse damage halo call it 3-5%. So it does NOT run "across most of the frame width" and does not reach x=0.70-0.90 -- it terminates around x~0.70. The speckle beyond x~0.80 in the ridge image is amplified noise in the near-zero-signal dark edge, not crack. The reviewer's 2-3% area estimate is about right.

Overprediction: SEVERE, worse than "severely" suggests. Red = 126,465 px inside the specimen = 64.8% of specimen area (63.4% of the whole panel). Per-column red fraction rises to 0.89-0.92 for the entire right half (x>0.5) as one solid block. The overlay on the normalized image shows that block sitting exactly on (a) the smooth right-ward illumination/thickness falloff and (b) the vertical mosaic tile seams -- both explicitly non-crack. Diagnostic proof the model is just thresholding raw brightness: mean raw gray inside red = 76 vs 167 outside; 90.4% of the darkest raw quartile is red while only 9.6% of the brightest quartile is. That is a global intensity threshold, not local-contrast crack detection.

red_floods_nonspecimen: CONFIRMED. 6,105 red px fall outside the specimen (raw gray <= 8), where the red rectangle's flat top and bottom edges overrun the specimen's slanted boundary into the black frame border.

False-positive fraction: even crediting the model with all ~5% of specimen area as crack-plus-halo (and only 81% of the ridge pixels are actually covered by red), true positives are at most ~8,000 of 126,465 red px, i.e. ~6% correct -> ~0.94-0.96 false positive. I use 0.95.

Usability: I do not agree the frame is unusable, which matches the reviewer's usable=true. The raw image contains an unambiguous, well-connected branching crack with clean local contrast -- it is one of the more valuable frames to hand-label. What is unusable is the prediction as a pseudo-label: it would need ~95% of its red erased, so it must not be fed back as-is into retraining.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260620_b3_3_0lbf_268_13um_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim

findings.notes: THIS IS THE HEADLINE FAILURE. Predicted crack area 87.6% (measured red 0.870): the model paints the entire black field red and leaves only the bright top-left blob unlabeled - it has literally inverted into a 'dark = crack' brightness threshold. Mean gray under the red mask is 3.5/255, i.e. it is labeling pure void as crack. Two independent reasons this is a guaranteed false positive: (1) the frame contains no specimen, and (2) the name is '3_0lbf' - zero applied load, an UNDAMAGED baseline, so the true crack area should be ~0. Recommend excluding 55.png from the dataset entirely and adding an automatic pre-filter that rejects frames whose mean intensity or fraction-of-nonblack falls below a threshold (e.g. reject if >70% of pixels < 20/255), since a single frame like this contributes ~0.87 area fraction and will badly distort any aggregate metric.

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260618_B2_2_1_lbf_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of005.xrm.bim.bim

findings.name: Average_mosaic_260619_HC_316L_fatigue_1400_cycles_tip_idx00000_mosaictileAA_img001of010.xrm.bim.bim

A single global brightness threshold (I<155) reproduces 84.5% of the red mask pixel-for-pixel, confirming the model is thresholding illumination, not detecting cracks. High-pass local texture std collapses from 10.1 (leftmost sixth) to 1.9 (rightmost sixth), i.e. the flooded region is flat and featureless with no elongated structures to find. 14.8% of the frame is genuinely near-black out-of-field (top-right corner plus a strip along the right edge, visible as a noise-amplified boundary in a flat-fielded version), and 72% of that out-of-field area is painted red. Frame is usable for training but needs an out-of-field mask on the right/top-right AND per-image flat-field correction before labels are trustworthy.
